hook.text: When the Jaguar E-Type debuted in 1961, Enzo Ferrari called it the most beautiful car ever made.

buildup.text: Its long hood, curved fenders, and sleek body were designed by aerodynamicist Malcolm Sayer.

discovery.text: It could hit 150 mph and cost half as much as its closest competitor—a stunning bargain.

twist.text: British build quality let it down. Electrical problems and overheating plagued early owners.

climax.text: Despite its flaws, the E-Type became the most iconic British car ever and a permanent design benchmark.

punchline.text: Beauty forgives a lot of electrical problems.

quiz.question: Who called the E-Type the most beautiful car ever made?

details.summary: The Jaguar E-Type, launched in 1961, was called the most beautiful car ever made by Enzo Ferrari himself, combining stunning looks with 150 mph performance at a fraction of Ferrari's price.
details.whyItMatters: The E-Type democratized sports car performance, offering Ferrari-level speed and beauty to a wider audience and cementing British automotive design in the global imagination.
takeaways: Enzo Ferrari called it the most beautiful car ever made
It could reach 150 mph, extraordinary for its era
At half the price of comparable Ferraris, it was a relative bargain

faq.question: How fast was the E-Type for its time?
faq.answer: Its 150 mph top speed matched or exceeded cars costing several times more. In 1961, only a handful of the most exotic and expensive supercars could keep up with the E-Type on the open road.

faq.question: Is the E-Type still collectible today?
faq.answer: Extremely. Early Series 1 models in good condition sell for hundreds of thousands of dollars. They are considered one of the most desirable classic cars and regularly top collector surveys.
